description: Canonical digest suite vocabulary for v1 typed digest values. A digest suite is the registered tuple (canonicalization, hash_algorithm), and canonical_id is the wire prefix in `<suite>:<lowercase_hex>` values. Event, Realm-derived and RealmCommit content-address identities are a separate fixed current-v1 domain and always use json_jcs + SHA-256 (suite code 0x01); no Realm field selects or transitions that suite.
suite_id_grammar: suite_id = hash_id | canonicalization_id '.' hash_id ; each segment matches [a-z0-9_]+ ; at most one dot. In the v1 canonical grammar, a bare hash_id denotes canonicalization=json_jcs.
registry_rules: A digest suite is an explicit canonicalization/hash tuple; only active rows are valid on wire.
Unknown suites in critical Event, RealmCommit, stream-head, receipt, or content-addressed digest fields fail closed.
Producer Event, Event-derived object and RealmCommit identities always use fixed_v1_content_address_suite; any other suite code in those typed IDs fails closed as unsupported_digest_algorithm.

Other typed domains such as Blob content addressing MAY select any suite whose active row and owning schema explicitly allow it; a new suite requires conformance vectors and MUST NOT silently widen Event or RealmCommit identity.

hash_strength_order.note: Performance-side order; v1 treats registered hashes as equal collision strength. Extended when post-quantum or diversity hashes are registered.

canonicalizations.definition: Arkret canonical JSON (RFC 8785 / JCS narrowed profile), zh/conformance/encoding.md §2.
canonicalizations.notes: Implied by bare (dot-free) suite ids; never written as an explicit dotted prefix segment in v1.

canonicalizations.definition: CBOR deterministic encoding (RFC 8949 §4.2) under the Arkret profile to be pinned by ak.profile.encoding.cbor.v1 (encoding rules, CDDL, schema-agnostic JSON<->CBOR type mapping, conformance vectors).
canonicalizations.notes: Reserved until ak.profile.encoding.cbor.v1 is fully specified. The mapping MUST be schema-agnostic (JSON string -> CBOR text string, JSON integer -> CBOR integer); canonicalization MUST NOT depend on schema knowledge.

suites.security_note: Fixed current-v1 Event, Event-derived object and RealmCommit identity suite; all receivers MUST support it. SHA-2 family, not post-quantum but Grover-degraded strength remains acceptable.
Best throughput (parallelizable); recommended for blob CID and high-volume paths.

suites.kat_absence_reason: Deterministic CBOR encoding and per-suite digest vectors are not published until all activation_requirements are complete.
activation_requirements: ak.profile.encoding.cbor.v1 fully specified: deterministic encoding rules pinned by directly adopting an upstream standardized deterministic CBOR profile (CDE, draft-ietf-cbor-cde, or dCBOR, draft-mcnally-deterministic-cbor) under draft-pinning discipline (draft change = new profile version) rather than a bespoke ruleset, CDDL for envelope and canonical objects, schema-agnostic JSON<->CBOR type mapping
Per-suite conformance vectors published for every typed domain that opts into CBOR
suites.security_note: Deterministic CBOR canonicalization with SHA-256. Same hash strength as sha256; any future activation is domain-specific and does not change current-v1 Event, Realm or RealmCommit identity.
